dedupe_keys.name: a review of cybersecurity incidents in the water sector fifteen documented incidents asce journal of environmental engineering 2020

description: This peer-reviewed review by researchers from Texas A&M, Singapore and Technion assembles fifteen disclosed and documented malicious cybersecurity incidents in the water sector, drawn from sources ranging from federal investigation reports to scientific papers. For each incident it compiles the situation, the response, the remediation and the lessons learned, and sets them against industrial control system architectures, attack-defence models and security solutions. It concludes that the frequency, diversity and complexity of threats to the water sector are rising, with new threats such as ransomware and cryptojacking alongside recurring weaknesses such as insider threats, and it calls for an adaptive, cooperative water cyberdefence. Coverage: fifteen incidents mostly in the United States, up to the paper's date. Access: a free preprint, with the licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: the incident list is a sample of disclosed cases and stops before the more recent ransomware waves. It supports cyber-physical scenario design for water utilities and relates to the Risevatnet dam valve attack case study and the BattLeDIM benchmark in the catalogue.
